question: Where is Morgan Stanley investing in technology for its advisors?

claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm has been investing over multiple years in its processes and systems to have robust infrastructure for growth, including technology, a better understanding of its data, and better servicing of clients, in the context of the Wealth Management platform.

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said the firm is investing in E*TRADE, and that financial advisors see the integrated firm as offering "unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating." The CFO said the firm has been investing in its self-directed platform, including marketing, and cited benefits from platform investments made over multiple years.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Pick described "ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel" as an engine for future growth.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), the CFO said early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot, are showing progress. She named DevGen AI (developer efficiency by modernizing code), Parable (an interactive data analysis and summarization tool), and LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors. Pick said the mantra is to scale with key clients, build out product capabilities and invest in technologies, some efficiency-driven and some effectiveness-driven.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Pick said the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities and Investment Management "via human capital and technology," and that its growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise. He said the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

On the same 4Q25 call (January 2026), a company representative said LeadIQ is helping introduce advisors to clients interested in advice using AI, and that technology on the revenue and expense sides should help drive margin.

The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) states that the Wealth Management segment's ability to compete across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels is affected by multiple factors, including "our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Pick said the firm's strategy is, in part, "to invest in our clients and technology across the integrated firm." He called AI platforms additive to what the firm has: world-class technology, world-class cyber defense, and trusted advisers sitting with the client, which he called the key.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Pick said the firm has built advantages around its self-directed channel, workplace offering and adviser-client relationships that "make technology a differentiator in our favor."

adjacent.text: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said AI tools are in use in the businesses, for example in equities where salespeople have different AI tools, and that productivity is real and "that's where a lot of the spend is being seen."
adjacent.differs_because: It describes AI spend in the equities (Institutional Securities) business, not technology for financial advisors, and gives no amount.

adjacent.text: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Pick described a client agent inside the electronic trading platform in the equities business, and AI efficiency in core infrastructure operations and surveillance.
adjacent.differs_because: These examples are in equities and infrastructure, not advisor tools.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley does not state a dollar amount or budget for technology investment aimed at financial advisors, or a ranked list of advisor-technology priorities, in the evidence provided. Management describes investment areas only qualitatively.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley investor day or Wealth Management deck, 10-K technology and expense discussion, or management commentary on technology spend
